title: A grid size you choose is the grid you get, one even grid at every zoom
goal: Setting the grid to four points does not give a four point grid. The canvas draws several densities at once, thinning and thickening as you zoom, so what you see is a wash of lines at spacings you never asked for. A size you choose should mean exactly that: one even grid, the same everywhere, at every zoom. The several-densities behaviour belongs only to the automatic setting, where following the zoom is the whole point. The lines should also be fainter than they are, so a fine grid sits behind the work instead of shouting over it. And while dragging the size slider, the label that says automatic should show the size being chosen, rather than a column of numbers beside the track that do not line up with the positions.
notes: Reported by the user on 2026-09-06: set grid sizes do not work, at four points they see a bunch of lines that are not four points apart. Confirmed by reading: CanvasGridSettings.liveSpacing (CanvasGrid.swift line 188) and the drawing both call CanvasGridLevels.levels, which returns up to maximumLevels of three rungs chosen from the zoom whatever the person set, so an explicit spacing is only ever the FINEST rung and two coarser ones are drawn with it. The ladder exists for a good reason and the user has now named where it belongs: only under automatic, which already exists as CanvasGridCellStops.automatic and is read through cellIsAutomatic (line 207). So the change is to branch, not to delete: a chosen size draws one spacing, automatic keeps the ladder. That also collapses most of snapping-pulls-to-the-grid-you-can-see-not-one-y for the chosen case, since drawn and set become the same thing; read that task and say in the audit what remains of it under automatic. Transparency: maximumOpacity is 0.30 (line 284); pick a lower number by looking at a fine grid zoomed in, not by taste alone, and keep it readable on a dark and a light picture. The slider labels are the tool bar's cell popup from the-grid-tool-bar-is-two-buttons-and-adjust-mode; if that task has not landed yet, coordinate rather than building the popup twice.
acceptance: With a size chosen, exactly one grid is drawn, at that spacing, at every zoom, with no second or third density behind it
The bolder line every so often may stay, since that is one grid emphasised rather than a second grid, and the audit says which reading was taken
With automatic chosen, the grid follows the zoom as it does now, and that is the only setting where the density changes on its own
The lines are fainter than today, checked at a fine spacing zoomed in, where the wash is worst, and still visible on both a light and a dark picture
Dragging the size slider shows the size being chosen where the automatic label sits, and the loose column of numbers beside the track is gone
Snapping pulls to the one grid drawn, which with a chosen size is simply that size at every zoom
A grid so fine it would be a solid wash at the current zoom is handled deliberately rather than by drawing mud; the audit says what happens and why
Core logic covered by tests in PhotonzCore written before the change, asserting one spacing out at several zooms for a chosen size
Audit written under queue/audits/ with a four point grid at three zooms, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) The ladder is right for automatic and wrong for a chosen size: a chosen size is a promise about the picture, and today the promise is broken in the one case a person can check by counting. Branch, do not delete. (2) A first-time user who picks 4 pt and then zooms out to 50% will find the grid gone under the new rule, because 4 pt at 50% is two screen points and there is nothing honest to draw. That is the one place this change can read as broken; it goes in the audit as a question rather than being papered over with a coarser grid nobody asked for. (3) The nine numbers beside the size slider are decoration: the slider already has nine stops and the button already says the size. One readout at the foot says more with less, and it is the thing the user asked for. (4) Shortest version: one branch, in CanvasGridSettings.levels(atZoom:), which the drawing, the pull and the readouts all go through, plus one new drawing rule and one lower opacity. No new settings, no new mode.

Reading taken on the bold line (acceptance 2): it stays. A bold every N lands ON lines the chosen grid already draws, so it adds emphasis, never a new line position. It fades in and out with the fine grid rather than outliving it, so there is never a moment where the only thing on screen is a density nobody chose.

Built. CanvasGridSettings.levels(atZoom:) is the one branch: automatic runs CanvasGridLevels.levels as before, a chosen size runs the new CanvasGridLevels.chosenLevels, which returns exactly the chosen spacing plus its bold every N at the same strength. The drawing (CanvasGridChrome), the pull (snapSpacing) and the readouts (liveSpacing, spacingChipText, cellButtonHelp) all read that one call, so they cannot disagree. Tests first in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/GridChosenSizeTests.swift, 15 cases, sweeping 400 zooms across the whole range for every stop on the slider.

Strength: maximumOpacity 0.30 -> 0.16, picked by looking at a four point grid at 100% in the probe rather than by taste. Measured off the real capture: fine lines now sit 40 levels off a white picture (was 62) and the bold ones about twice that.

One thing the task did not ask for but its fourth acceptance item forced: the grid ink was resolved against the WINDOW appearance, so it went near black in light and near white in dark. At the new lower strength that left the lines four levels off a white picture in the dark appearance, and invisible over a dark screenshot in the light one. It is now one mid tone, so it reads on a light picture and a dark one in either appearance. Measured both.

The too-fine case (acceptance 7): a chosen size fades out as its lines close on four screen points and is gone by two, and nothing coarser replaces it. Seeing it at 50% in the probe, a lit switch and a set size over an empty canvas reads as a bug, so the size button now dims and its tooltip says the grid is too fine to draw here and to zoom in. CanvasGridSettings.cellIsTooFineToDraw(atZoom:), tested.

Slider: the nine numbers beside the track are gone; the track keeps nine invisible pressable rows (so a press still lands on a size, and walks can still name one) and one readout under it where Auto used to sit, showing whatever is being chosen. Note for anyone touching it: .offset does NOT move a view's layout frame, so the first attempt registered all nine rows at the same point and every press picked the same size; they are laid out in a VStack now, with the rail over them and hit testing off.

Verified in the probe with Scripts/playtest/grid-chosen-size-walk.json: at 4 pt the grid report says 2 rungs and pulls to 4 at 100%, 200% and 400%; at 50% it says nothing drawn; at 16 pt it pulls to 16; automatic still says 3 rungs and pulls to 32 at 100%. Full suite green, 4240 tests. Every other grid walk still passes; grid-origin-walk was already broken on a control removed by the tool bar task, filed as the-grid-origin-walk-drives-the-buttons-the-tool.
